Because of the explosive charge, there is a small area of lethality directly behind the mine, as well as the area of devastation in front of the blast.

text_en: The M67 fragmentation hand grenade is the current U.S. Army-issue hand grenade. It is lethal to 5 meters, and is capable of causing casualties out to 15 meters. It consists of an explosive charge, which is contained in a steel shell. The shell shatters into fragments when the grenade explodes. The timer in the grenade will cause it to explode between 3 and 5 seconds after the spoon is released from the body of the device.

text_zh: OICW 即"理想单兵战斗武器"， 是一种正在接受美军测试、 有望列装的武器系统。 它由两部分组成：一支可发射 M16 系列现用 5.56x45mm 枪弹的突击 步枪，以及一门 20mm 半自动榴弹发射器。 榴弹发射器身管装在步枪身管上 方，使用无托布局， 供弹具位于武器后部，容弹 6 发。两部分可以分离， 较轻的步枪部分可脱离榴弹发射 器单独使用。
text_en: The OICW, or Objective Individual Combat Weapon, is a weapons system that is currently being tested for possible implementation by the U.S. Army. The weapons system consists of an assault rifle capable of firing the 5.56 x 45 mm ammunition currently used by the M16 family of weapons and a 20 mm semi-automatic grenade launcher. The grenade launcher barrel is mounted above the rifle barrel, and the launcher loads from a 6 round magazine near the rear of the weapon in a bullpup configuration. The two systems can be separated, and the lighter, assault rifle-only portion can be used independently of the grenade launcher.
text_edited: OICW 即"理想单兵战斗武器"， 是一种正在接受美军测试、 有望列装的武器系统。 它由两部分组成：一支可发射 M16 系列现用 5.56x45mm 枪弹的突击 步枪，以及一门 20mm 半自动榴弹发射器。 榴弹发射器身管装在步枪身管上 方，使用无托布局， 供弹具位于武器后部，容弹 6 发。两部分可以分离， 较轻的步枪部分可脱离榴弹发射 器单独使用。

text_zh: M136 是一种一次性无后座力武器 系统，发射 84mm 破甲火箭弹， 可摧毁轻装甲车辆。破甲弹可穿透 420mm 装甲。除破甲弹外，M136 还可发射穿深高达 600mm 的高穿透弹，足以击穿大多数主战 坦克的装甲。 幽灵小队使用的 M136 装有瞄准镜， 便于士兵放大锁定目标。
text_en: The M136 is a disposable recoilless weapons system that fires an 84 mm HEAT (High Explosive Anti-Tank) rocket capable of destroying light armored vehicles. The HEAT round is capable of penetrating 420 mm of armor. In addition to the HEAT round, the M136 is capable of firing a HP (High Penetration) round that is capable of penetrating up to 600 mm of armor, which is sufficient to penetrate the armor of most main battle tanks.  The M136 available to the Ghosts is equipped with a scope to allow soldiers to zoom in on their targets.

text_en: The AN/GSQ-187 sensor is a placed remote sensor that can pick up enemy movements based upon several types of input. It can then process this information, and relay to a computer the location, speed, and direction of travel of the units passing through the area.  It is even capable of determining the difference between tracked and wheeled vehicles through seismic data.

Sniper
"Why yes, I did shoot him. And him. And her. And the car. It seemed the appropriate response, considering the circumstances."

History
Born September 30, 1975 in Kensington, London. Father (Thomas) was retired from diplomatic service, mother (Claudine, d. 1990) was French national. Family lived comfortably off investments. Attended Southbank International School as a charter student. Studied for two years at Oxford. Dropped out of school and enlisted in 1996. Scored highest marks ever recorded on initial marksmanship test. Trained as a sniper. Recruited by SAS in 2000. Saw first field action in 2003 as part of advance force sent in during Eritrea peacekeeping mission. Captured by guerillas November 3, 2003. Escaped and killed his captors November 6, 2003, and walked 45 km to friendly territory. Reassigned and attached to Ghosts March 16, 2005.

Stone is quiet, methodical and efficient - perfect traits for a sniper. He speaks English and French with equal facility, as his parents spoke both at home and insisted he be fluent in each. His relationship with his father is cool at best, as he suspects his father has tried to arrange favors for him rather than let him advance on his own merits. Stone is something of a straight arrow, as he does not drink or smoke (though he does play poker, which he regards as an exercise in applied mathematics, with devastating efficiency). His sense of humor is dry to the point of being arid, and no one - especially not Stone himself - is safe from his acid wit. Rodriguez is perhaps his best friend among the Ghosts, but even he can't get Stone to discuss his experiences in Eritrea.

History
Born February 7, 1973 in Gori, GSR. Father (Georgi, d. 1994) and mother (Irina, d. 1992) were government bureaucrats. Joined Georgian army in 1991, shortly after independence. Was involved in botched attempts to transport displaced Abkhaz civilians, later saw action against Abkhazi irregulars. Trained in heavy weapons usage, specializing in anti-tank operations. Saw additional action in Ajaria and the Javakheti district, including facing Russian "observers" on two occasions. Stayed loyal to central Georgian government and took part in several actions against independent militias. Attached to Ghosts in 2002 as part of an increased cooperative effort between the United States and Georgia.

Osadze is fiercely patriotic toward his homeland, and has a long-standing resentment against anyone - Abkhaz, Russian, Ossetian or anyone else - who would move against it. His parents were career bureaucrats who were instrumental in the transition from Soviet Republic to independence, instilling in their son an unshakable loyalty to the idea of a free Georgia. Georgi Osadze was later gunned down by members of one of the many unaffiliated militias that sprang into being in the early 1990s, and this fact is never far from Guram's mind. Guram has a particular dislike for the Russian military, which he blames for fostering dissent in the autonomous regions of Georgia. Off-duty, he is friendly, gregarious and boisterous, even going so far as to get Cpt. Grey to crack the odd smile. Osadze's English is poor, but rapidly improving. He has few interests outside of his work and regional politics, but he will passionately debate anyone so foolish as to bring up the topic. However, he does have a particular weakness for American rap music, which he insists on playing at ear-splitting volume.

Support
"If you keep talking while I am trying to work, we are both going to end up dead. Get back to me when you've made a decision as to which choice you would prefer."

Medical
D.O.B.: June 4, 1971
Height: 5'11" (180 cm)
Weight: 195 lbs (88 kg)
Hair: Sandy blonde
Eyes: Blue
Gender: M
Distinguishing Characteristics: Index finger of right hand has been repeatedly broken and the fractures have not healed cleanly. Finger is 1.5 cm shorter than it should be as a result.

History
Born June 4, 1971 in Emden. Father (Meier, d. 2007) and mother (Helena) both worked for local shipping company. Exceptional student, demonstrated an early aptitude for chemistry. Majored in Chemical Engineering at University of Applied Sciences in Emden. Graduated 1992. Spent two years working in R&D for container manufacturer, also in Emden. Enlisted in Bundeswehr November, 1994. Received training in Demolitions. Served with UN force in Kosovo. Later assigned to German-American Corps. Attached to Ghosts in August, 2003.

Henkel is methodical almost to a fault. He is precise in word and deed, and never acts without assessing the situation from all angles. Unlike Tunney, he takes no glee in the more flamboyant aspects of his work, preferring instead the quiet satisfaction of a job well done. Henkel is such a perfectionist, however, that he rarely regards any job as well done, least of all his own. Such constant nitpicking often gets on the nerves of new members of the Ghosts until they get more comfortable with him, at which point it becomes white noise. It's only when he stops finding faults in a situation that they start to worry. Speaking heavily accented English as well as German, Henkel is one of the least talkative members of the Ghosts, though he's more social than his countryman Munz. A devotee of classical music, Henkel spends his off hours reading technical journals and listening to his prized collection of classical CDs. However, he still maintains that records provide better sound quality, and anyone attempting to argue will be in for a very long discussion.

History

Two younger brothers, Henry (b. 1981) and Travis (b. 1983). 4 year starter on high school baseball team, drafted 32nd round in 1992 amateur draft by Cincinnati Reds. Responsible for retrieving 2 UN personnel taken prisoner by Macedonian nationals, and received commendation for his efforts. Promoted to Captain February 1998. Assigned to Ghosts in 2001.

Jacobs has an undeniable charisma, which is one of his greatest assets in the field. A keen student of tactics, he puts his troops in a position to succeed. They know this, and fight harder for him as a result. He is soft-spoken (except when in the field) and extremely analytical, and has a reputation as a chess shark that extends far outside the Ghosts. Among his interests are music (he is an accomplished pianist) and astronomy, and Jacobs will neither confirm nor deny that he is in fact a Mensa member. Jacobs also speaks Cantonese fluently, though his attempts at Russian and Japanese have both been described by native speakers as "interesting." Jacobs has never married, but he is extremely close to his father and both of his younger brothers. That sort of relationship also extends to the Ghosts, where he is the unquestioned hub around which the unit revolves. Jacobs has already expressed an interest in politics as a post-military career, and his success thus far bodes well for his chances.

Born August 17, 1983 in Modesto, CA. Father (Enrique, d. 1985) was a construction foreman, killed in an onsite accident. Mother (Beatriz) worked a variety of jobs, remarried in 1987. Born in a Spanish-speaking household, Ramirez is fluent in both Spanish and English. After his father's death, his mother moved around frequently, which, combined with Henry's small size, ensured that he was consistently getting picked on by larger students. As a result, he rapidly got very good at running and hiding, as well as cheap-shotting his tormentors when he had a chance. Henry has a very cool relationship with his stepfather, and has not spoken to his family for four years as a result. He is soft-spoken, and is very sensitive about being shown proper "face." Ramirez has a particular dislike for short jokes, being called "Hank," or otherwise being shown disrespect, and will carry a grudge, though never into the field. He has few friends in the unit, but is extremely loyal to those few - particularly Stone and Jacobs - he is close to.

"I was too old for this crap twenty years ago. You can imagine how much I'm enjoying it now."

History
Born March 17, 1955 in Jefferson City, MO. Father (Thomas, d. 1984) and mother (Augusta) both worked on the family farm. Two-sport star in high school, made All-State in football as a quarterback. Attended West Point (Class of 1975) and stood fifteenth in his class. Entered service with 82nd Airborne just after the retreat from Saigon. Made Captain in 1979 and transferred to Special Forces. Was part of the attempted rescue of American hostages at the U.S. embassy in Teheran in 1980, which was his first field operation with Special Forces. Served with distinction in Haiti and Panama. Attached to U.S. forces in Mogadishu. Stationed for four years in Germany. Was one of the first soldiers assigned to the Ghosts when they were formed in 1994. Commands the assault unit.

Gordon speaks just enough German to be able to order a beer, and otherwise has little use for anything made outside of the U.S.A. Fiercely patriotic, he is married to his career and to the unit. He is savagely protective of his people and will not send them in unless there's a damn good reason to do so - and a good chance they'll be coming out the other side. The soldiers under his command refer to him as "The Old Man" and would willingly run through a brick wall for him (though Cohen would prefer to blow it up on his behalf instead). He never asks his people to go anyplace he won't, and has a bad habit of taking point on occasion. Gordon has an encyclopedic knowledge of military history and a wealth of personal experience, and it is rare that he finds himself in a situation for which he has no precedent. His persona is aggressively gruff, and he has no patience for slackers, shirkers or anyone who isn't up to his extremely high standards for the Ghosts.

Born June 4, 1982 in Taurage, Lithuania. Father (Darius, labor exchange administrator) and mother (Lydie, doctor) met at youth sports camp under Soviet regime. Initially trained in swimming but was deemed incapable of performing at competitive international level. Took up shooting while in school under father's tutelage. Excelled early at biathlon. History
Born July 22, 1981 in Massapequa, Long Island, NY. Real name Leah, known as "Lindy" since elementary school. Father (Bernard) is a dentist, mother (Harriette) a schoolteacher. Graduated 2nd in her high school class. Scored 99% across the board on New York State Regents Exam. Accepted to Barnard, Mt. Holyoke and Sarah Lawrence but instead enlisted in 1999. Assigned to Signals and was attached to the 10th Infantry. Served with distinction in peacekeeping operations in Eritrea (2003) and East Timor (2004). Transferred to MacDill AFB and attached to Special Forces there. Requested and received transfer to Ghosts in 2005 as part of a program exploring the possibility of having women serve in front-line units. Assault specialist. Has repeatedly won awards for marksmanship, but has a particular fondness for unarmed combat. Put an unarmed combat instructor in the infirmary during basic, which made her extremely popular with her fellow trainees. Has a preference for the M203 grenade launcher, and is extremely skilled in its use.

Cohen speaks English and Spanish fluently, with a smattering of other languages including Hebrew, French and German. She is very forceful in discussion; once she settles on a decision, that's it. Lindy has what has been described as "an excess of enthusiasm" in the field, and has been known to run out of ammunition on occasion as a result. She carries an optimistic attitude with her into any situation, regardless of how dire circumstances might seem, and this approach rubs off on her squadmates. Cohen is not shy about expressing her opinion, but is meticulous about making sure she knows what she's talking about before she opens her mouth. She is perhaps the most popular member of the Ghosts, and many of her squadmates regard her as almost a kid sister. Perhaps the one blemish on her record is a long-standing dispute with Cpt. Susan Grey, whom Cohen refers to as "Her Majesty."

Born November 11, 1968 in Stuttgart, Germany. Father (Helmut, d. 1989) was an automobile mechanic, mother (Ilse, d. 1994) worked in retail. Achieved average marks in school. Spent much of his free time working with his father and achieved a high degree of technical expertise. Spent two years working as an auto mechanic before joining Border Police. Munz is still uncomfortable working with most of the other Ghosts, and spends what little social time he takes with Fw. Klaus Henkel, the other German attached to the unit.

Gender: Male

History
Born September 11, 1980, in Thorpe Salvin, Yorkshire. Working-class upbringing. Father (Ian) ran a petrol station, mother (Isobel) taught preschool. Father served in British Army 1974-1978; saw duty in Northern Ireland. Frequently in trouble with school and legal authorities. Cited for shoplifting, vandalism and other minor offenses repeatedly. Excelled in chemistry in school. Was expelled (1997) for prank gone wrong which resulted in demolition of school's chemistry laboratory and slight injuries to two teachers. Enlisted shortly thereafter. Natural aptitude for explosives became obvious during basic training. Was assigned to EOD and served with distinction. Disciplined several times for "unconventional approach." Recruited by SAS in 2001 and trained in demolitions. Defused ULA-planted explosives at Gatwick in 2004 and won national acclaim; later used [over strenuous objections] in recruiting campaign as "the face of the new army." Attached to Ghosts in 2005.

Nigel Tunney threatens to quit approximately once every three weeks. He is loud, brash, and as much of a free spirit as a member of SAS dares to be. On one memorable occasion, he reported after leave with his hair dyed bright pink. Tunney parties hard but works harder, and constantly keeps one eye on his father's service record as a benchmark for his own achievements. He is gregarious, aggressively friendly, and rarely takes "no" for an answer. When working, he is absolutely meticulous, and all traces of his off-duty persona disappear, except for the predilection for peppering every sentence with profanity. Tunney is a die-hard Blackburn Rovers fan, and defends the side's honor more aggressively than he defends his own.

History
Born September 6, 1980 in the Denden region. Father (Essaias, d. 2001) and mother (Mebrat) were both EPLF (Eritrean People's Liberation Front) fighters. Father was instrumental in the liberation of Asmara in 1991. After Eritrean independence was established in 1993, family settled in Asmara. Family moved into politics, with both parents serving in Eritrean government. Was sent abroad for schooling in 1994. Stayed in England for school until resumption of hostilities with Ethiopia in 1997. Younger sister, Asmert (d. 2000) killed by Ethiopian bombing.

Against parents' wishes, enlisted in Army. Served with distinction during border flare-ups from 1997-2000. Promoted twice. Wounded in leg during skirmish near Sheshebit. Promoted again at opening of formal hostilities in 2000. Served under her father, who was killed in action in Badme. Served with distinction until World Court-mandated cessation of hostilities in 2002. Stayed in active service and was promoted twice more during interim. Attached unofficially to the Ghosts after the landing near Massawa.

Haile is fiercely devoted to Eritrea and to the memory of her father. She has an encyclopedic knowledge of the historical conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea, and will gladly argue her position for as long as it takes. Extremely focused on her work, she has little time for social graces, and has a reputation for being extremely direct and to the point. This has made her some enemies in the halls of power in Asmara, but won her the admiration of the troops she has served with. She has little patience for time-wasters and politicians, but a great respect for those who have served in the field. Haile has a surprising taste for Indian food and music, which she picked up during her school years. However, the memory of her youth in the Denden trench complexes is something that has never left her, and she is more comfortable in the field than she is surrounded by the comforts of home.

Sniper

History

Recruited into Special Forces and assigned to MacDill AFB in 2005. Assigned to Ghosts in July, 2007.

Ibrahim is the newest member of the Ghosts, and as such is anxious to prove himself. He has a tendency to talk too much when he's nervous, and has been dubbed "Class Nerd" by Gordon. When relaxed, Ibrahim is something of a practical joker, though he generally shows restraint when it comes to the timing of his operations. He is tall and appears a bit gangly, but regularly posts the best time for the mile in the unit. Speaking English with some Arabic and French, Ibrahim is also an excellent guitarist, though his singing voice is best left undescribed. When he can get away with it, Ibrahim wears a Minnesota Vikings cap that he's had for over ten years. He is also fond of talking about his girlfriend back home, though none of the other Ghosts have so much as seen a picture of her. In the field, Ibrahim has been described as "a sniper with the M136," as much for his accuracy as for his uncanny ability to position himself to be able to wreak devastation.

在 Tom Clancy 的幽灵行动中， 你是一支美军顶级步兵部队的一 员：第 5 特种作战群 1 营 D 连， 营地在北卡罗来纳州的布拉格堡。

队员从 4 个兵种中选出： 步枪手、 支援专家、 爆破专家和狙击手， 全部为上士，年近三十或三十出头 。

作为战场上幽灵排的指挥者， 你要负责挑选火力组成员、 为他们配备装备，并在交火开始后 指挥他们。战斗最激烈的时候由你 掌控他们 ，看着他们执行你的命令、 完成任务。

text_en:
Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon:  Who are the Ghosts?

In Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon, you are part of an elite American infantry unit; the 5th Special Forces Group, 1st Battalion, D Company operating out of Ft. Bragg, North Carolina.

Using the most advanced technology the United States has to offer, D company often finds itself on the front lines.  As the spearhead of the United States Army's quick response, they are the first unit deployed into dangerous situations and the last ones to leave when things get rough.  Due to their experience at striking "swiftly, silently and invisibly"; D Company is nicknamed "The Ghosts"

Individual team members are drawn from 4 soldier classes:  Riflemen, Support Experts, Demolition Experts, and Snipers.  All are Sergeants First Class in their late 20's or early 30's.

As the leader of a platoon of Ghosts in the field, it is your responsibility to select your fireteam members, equip them, and command them once the shooting starts. You control them during the heat of battle, as they seek to execute your orders, and complete missions.

Particularly spectacular performance and the completion of special objectives will unlock Specialist characters, who bring new weapons and new levels of expertise to your platoon.  These specialists may be other Special Forces soldiers, members of other branches of the U.S. military (Seals, Marines) or even foreign nationals on temporary assignment.

text_en:
Soldier Classes:

Assault:
The assault class is the standard infantry rifleman.  He carries the M16A2 weapons system, and has the option of attaching the M203 grenade launcher.  The assault soldier is dressed in a medium level of body armor.

Support:
The support class is armed with the M249 SAW (Squad Automatic Weapon), and provide mobile but intense firepower for their squad.  They are equipped with heavy armor to help deal with the greater amount of fire they are likely to receive in return. Because of the extra weight they carry around, the support class is also the toughest of the four classes of soldier.

Demolitions:
If something needs to be blown up, the demolitions class is the soldier of choice.  They are armed with the M4 carbine, and carry a variety of special gear from the M2 demolitions charge to the M136 anti-tank rocket.  These soldiers are equipped with a medium level of body armor.

Sniper:
The sniper class is the master of the long-range kill.  Armed with the M24 sniper rifle, and their knowledge of stealthy movement, the sniper can sneak into a location that overlooks the enemy, and methodically engage them.  Due to the range of the sniper's engagements, he is not expected to take direct heavy fire, and so is equipped with only light body armor to allow maximum mobility.

Specialist:
The Ghosts are trained to work with a wide variety of specialists and, when necessary, integrate them into operations.  These specialists generally have weapons of their own that differ from the standard Ghost loadout, ranging from the technologically advanced OICW to the lethal support of the MG3.

text_zh:
东线与俄罗斯战役

2005 年， 在国力下滑和军事上一再难堪 多年之后，俄罗斯民众把 Putin 赶下台， 换上极端民族主义激进分子 Dmitri Arbatov。 阿尔巴托夫总统随即中止国内自 由化措施，开始对有组织犯罪、 大公司和少数族群推行高压政策， 称他们是"黑帮、 掌权者和非俄罗斯 的祸根"。 与此同时，军队开销大大增加， 敢言的极端民族主义者被提升 到军官团各处的要职。维克托卡尔 平将军被任命为陆军大将， 并任国防部副部长。阿尔巴托夫和 卡尔平都公开宣称，要重建随苏维 埃制度崩溃而失去的旧日大国地 位。

白俄罗斯、Ukraine 和哈萨克斯坦的亲俄政 府迅速追随新俄罗斯。2007 年， 四国联合组成俄罗斯民主联盟 (RDU)。 其他前苏联加盟共和国内的极端 民族主义派系也开始要求加入。 维尔纽斯和塔林爆发骚乱--这里是 立陶宛和爱沙尼亚的首都。 格鲁吉亚爆发公开武装冲突， 极端民族主义游击队在北部和西 部与格鲁吉亚军队交战。

格鲁吉亚政府请求美国帮助平定 叛乱。美国不顾俄罗斯抗议， 向第比利斯派出 2000 名维和人员， 并开始从 Turkey 的北约基地出动战机， 打击游击队阵地。紧张局势升级三 周后， 俄罗斯入侵，大军越过格鲁吉亚边 境。阿尔巴托夫总统发表电视讲话 ，称俄罗斯需要"保护我们的边 界， 不受西方强权挑起的动乱侵扰 "。格鲁吉亚人和美军盟友很快被击 溃，初次进攻仅十二天后， 最后一架直升机就离开了美国在 第比利斯的使馆楼顶。

危机的焦点随即转向波罗的海--爱 沙尼亚、拉脱维亚和立陶宛同样在 乱局之中。大规模军事集结随之而 来：美国及其盟友把数十万部队部 署进波罗的海地区，俄罗斯则针锋 相对。阿尔巴托夫总统放话： "尽管外国强权机关算尽， 俄罗斯人仍将再次成为统一的人 民。"边境小冲突升级两个月后， 俄军于 2008 年年中发动全面入侵。

开战之初盟军节节败退， 但局势最后反转， 俄军攻势被挡住。6 月初维尔纽斯解放，俄国人几周前 才立起来的代理人政权随之垮台； 到 7 月，俄军全面溃退。

面对这场难看的败仗，俄罗斯民意 大举转向，反对阿尔巴托夫政权。 民众走上 Moscow 和 St. Petersburg 的街头， 要求他下台。 可他还没来得及动作 ，卡尔平将军 就替他动了--解除他的职务， 实施军事管制。极端民族主义阵线 的反对声音瞬间消失。抗议者被成 批射杀，反对者被大批关起来。

西方开始大规模削弱极端民族主 义者的权力根基。武器和资助被输 送到地下反对派，军事打击则只针 对亲极端民族主义的目标。 随着天气转冷，极端民族主义者的 阵地在全国土崩瓦解，只剩莫斯科 周边地区作为他们最后的地盘。 俄军的忠诚派与极端民族主义派 在城北数百英里处打了一场决定 性的大战，美军协助忠诚派作战。 极端民族主义者赢了--但靠的是在 战场上引爆一枚战术原子弹， 此举让他们彻底背上国际罪犯的 名声。当美军与忠诚派联军向红场 合围、准备端掉缩在克里姆林宫地 堡里的卡尔平将军时，数以百万计 的平民逃离了 Moscow。
text_en:
The Eastern European and Russian Campaigns

In 2005, after years of economic decline and military humiliation the Russian people throw Vladimir Putin out of office and replace him with Ultranationalist extremist Dmitri Arbatov.  President Arbatov immediately freezes liberal reforms within Russia's borders and begins an aggressive policy of repression against organized crime, big business, and ethnic minorities: "gangsters, oligarchs, and non-Russian parasites."  Simultaneously he pushes through a drastic increase in funding for the military, promoting outspoken Ultranationalists to positions of power throughout the officer corps. General Viktor Karpin is appointed General of the Army and Deputy Defense Minister.  Both Arbatov and Karpin are quoted publicly that they intend to rebuild the empire that was lost with the fall of Communism.

Sympathetic governments in Belarus, Ukraine and Kazakhstan quickly fall in line with the new Russia.  In 2007 the four countries join together to form the Russian Democratic Union (RDU).  Ultranationalist factions within other former Soviet republics begin agitating for union as well.  Riots break out in Vilnius and Tallinn, the Lithuanian and Estonian capitals.  Georgia explodes into open armed combat with Ultranationalist guerrillas battling the Georgian army in the north and west.

The Georgian government appeals to the United States for help in putting down the rebellion.  Over Russian protests the U.S. sends 2000 peacekeepers to T'bilisi and begins flying air strikes against guerrilla positions out of NATO airbases in Turkey.  After three weeks of escalating tension Russia invades, sending troops pouring across the Georgian border.  President Arbatov delivers a televised address citing Russia's need to "protect our borders against unrest stirred up by unscrupulous Western powers."  The Georgians and their U.S. allies are quickly overwhelmed and the last helicopter leaves the roof of the U.S. embassy in T'bilisi only twelve days after the initial attack.

The focus of the crisis now shifts to the Baltic, where Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania are experiencing similar unrest.  A massive military build-up ensues, with the U.S. and its allies deploying hundreds of thousands of troops into the Baltic and Russia countering.  President Arbatov is quoted saying that "the Russians will once again be a unified people, despite the machinations of foreign imperialists."  After two months of escalating border skirmishes the Russians launch an all-out invasion of the Baltics in summer 2008.

At first the battle goes against the allies, but eventually the tide turns and the Russian advance is halted, Vilnius is liberated in early June, toppling the puppet government the Russians had installed only weeks before, and by July the Russians are in full retreat.

In the face of a humiliating defeat Russian public opinion turns sharply against the Arbatov administration.  Crowds take to the streets in Moscow and St. Petersburg demanding that he step down.  Before he can act, however, General Karpin acts for him, removing him from office and instituting martial law.  Instantly all opposition to the Ultranationalist cause is silenced.  Protesters are shot down en masse and the jails fill with political prisoners.

The West begins a massive campaign to undermine the Ultranationalist power base.  Arms and money are funneled to the underground opposition and military strikes are aimed only at targets friendly to the Ultranationalist cause.  As autumn sets in the Ultranationalist position is collapsing all over the country until only the area around Moscow remains as their last stronghold of power.  The Loyalists and Ultranationalist factions of the Russian Army fight a final massive battle several hundred miles north of the city, with U.S. troops aiding the Loyalists.  The Ultranationalists win, but only by detonating a tactical nuclear bomb on the battlefield, a move that cements their position as international criminals.  Civilians flee by the millions from Moscow as the combined U.S./Loyalist army converges on Red Square to crush General Karpin in his Kremlin bunker.

非洲战役：

俄罗斯大乱余波未平，世界各地又 接连爆发多场小规模战事。 其中最致命的，是埃塞俄比亚与厄 立特里亚战火又起。

两国关系刚刚缓和，就被一支背后 有 Sudan 支持的埃塞俄比 亚叛军打破。这批人从 Moscow 短命的旧政权手里取得大量武器， 发动政变。在 Tesfaye Wolde 上校指挥下， 他们夺取了亚的斯亚贝巴的控制 权，并立刻因出海口之争让国家重 新陷入与厄立特里亚的敌对。

埃军推进到 Assab 附近的海边， 夺取美国公司的工厂和设施据为 己有。埃塞俄比亚的攻势把厄立特 里亚军队压得连连后撤。 美国方面也因此被拖了进去： 战事已使红海大部分国际航运中 断。在一次事件中， 美国和其他国家 的运输舰在 Bab el Mandeb 以北遭到埃军岸基火 箭袭击。

混乱之中，一支小规模美国海军陆 战队被派去保护美国平民撤离。 当他们正把人员运出阿斯马拉时， 陆战队遭到推进中的埃军射击。 美方正式认错，但美国介入已成定 局。

与此同时，毁灭性的旱灾和随之而 来的灾荒再度袭来，厄立特里亚政 府早已请求联合国干预。 国际救援行动遭到武装分子的阻 拦，而且有有力证据表明这些武装 分子受新埃塞俄比亚政府支持。 为避免人道灾难，一个国际联盟建 立起来，联合国进场，美国领头。

他们公开宣布的任务是： 守住厄立特里亚边境，停止战斗， 确保救援物资送到灾民手中。

幽灵小队重返战场，担任这支部队 的先锋。他们的任务是替多国部队 开路，把入侵者赶回自己的边境。
text_en:
The African Campaign:

In the wake of the upheaval in Russia, a series of small brushfire wars erupt around the world. One of the deadliest is a resumption of hostilities between Ethiopia and Eritrea.

A growing détente between the two countries is disrupted by a band of Ethiopian insurgents with Sudanese backing. Having purchased massive amounts of weaponry from the short-lived reactionary government in Moscow, they mount a coup. Under the leadership of Col. Tesfaye Wolde, they seize control in Addis Ababa and immediately plunge the country into renewed hostilities with Eritrea over the issue of coastal access.

Ethiopian forces drive to the sea near Assab, seizing assets belonging to US companies and nationalizing them.  The Ethiopian offensive sends the Eritrean forces into hurried retreat.  US interests are also involved because the fighting has shut down most international shipping through the Red Sea. In one incident, American and other freighters were fired upon with shore rockets by Ethiopian troops north of the Bab el Mandeb.

In the wake of the chaos, a small force of US  Marines is deployed to guard the evacuation of US nationals. While they are getting people out of Asmara, the Marines come under fire from advancing Ethiopian troops. An official apology is made, but the stage has been set for US involvement.

All of this coincides with a recurrence of devastating drought and famine, which has already led to calls for UN intervention from the Eritrean government.  International efforts to provide famine relief are obstructed by bandits, and there's strong proof that these groups are backed by the new Ethiopian government.  In order to avert a humanitarian crisis, an international coalition is built and the UN goes in, with the US leading the way.

Their stated mandate is to secure the Eritrean border, stop the fighting, and make sure relief missions can get to the famine victims.

The Ghosts are back in action, spearheading this force. Their job is to lead the way for the multinational force and to help push the invading troops back to their own border.

开发手记：第一辑

达伦丘基图斯
制作人
幽灵行动
手记 1:

对幽灵行动团队来说，这个月相当 提气。我们完成了 Alpha 节点， 正向 Beta 全力推进。 这段时间里，我亲眼看着游戏按 团队认为能让它更出色的方向一 步步成型。我们还能把玩家和焦点 小组的意见带进会议，决定如何让 所有人满意。特别要感谢那些在留 言区和来信里给我们提意见的人。 我个人没多少机会去留言区发言， 但请转告大家：我们在听， 我们重视你们的每一条意见。 多谢！

格雷格斯特尔马克回到幽灵行动、 回到 RSE，让我开心极了。我曾在 RS Eagle Watch 项目里 与他共事， 深知他是团队和公司难 得的人才 。加上这一位，我们已经有 3 位斯特尔马克(我称他们为"可互换 的斯特尔 马克三人组")--我们的斯特 尔马克人数到顶了！

我刚从 Los Angeles 回来，为游戏录配音。Soundelux 的人一直待我们不薄--行内真正的 高手。幽灵行动的作曲家比尔布朗 赶着给我放了几段新配乐， 我们正把它们编进游戏主界面。 这声音简直再合适不过： 俄罗斯风格的乐器，混着美国传统 军乐的味道，比尔立下了游戏音乐 的新标杆。两场录音之间， 混音师达奇希尔架起几把吉他和 效果器，随手合了一曲。我可不是 Hendrix，但真是开心。 谢了，达奇！

好了，回去干活。我只想说， 全队正全力要给你们一部了不起 的游戏。我们会在留言区看你们的 发言。

罗比爱德华兹 - 副制作人
手记 1:

我们到达 Alpha 了。本月我们还对幽灵行 动做了焦点小组测试，接下来会分 析全部数据。眼下游戏十分扎实、 可玩性很高，我们正打算在 Beta 日期到来前补上最后几项特性。 我们给新闻界做了大量演示， 请留意各处网站上谈论幽灵行动 的文章。最让人受用的是， 音效材料基本到位，游戏里武器的 音效比以往任何时候都好。 另外，我们还加入了大量老玩家记 得的出色音乐，为游戏增色不少。 总之，全队对产品满心期待， 要把游戏完成好交给所有玩家。

德里克 L 厄尔伍德
测试分析员
Red Storm Entertainment
手记 1:

测试总算恢复了正常。两位测试组 长都上了手，项目里也有了几名测 试员，总算能干成点事了。 让新测试员上手大约要一周： 先是单调的流程，再来口头敲打、 超长工时，加上他们是在分文不取 地干活--这些会迅速击碎他们的心 防，让他们很快认同我们的想法。 这法子从来没失过手，对新来的几 位看起来也效果奇好。我的两位组 长克里斯和博正在成为此道高手。 他们让我无比自豪。

手记 2:

新测试员的调教接近完成。 他们大多数时候已经没有自己的 主意。我在他们眼里有时看到一丝 独立的微光，这让我有点担心， 但我相信那点光很快也会灭掉。 这种规模的项目测试要求不加分 辨地服从命令，我不会容许自作主 张的人。下一步他们可能就会要求 准点休 息、出去透气或者离开一下。 绝不容许。他们找到的 bug 数量， 越来越多，正与自主判断能力一同 离他们而去。

手记 3:

我听到一个测试员说，他们多么乐 意一遍遍测试几何和纹理。 这话真让我动容。克里斯和博干得 好。工程师和美术师看起来对新人 的活很满意。等下一次认证到来， 我相信测试员们这种不问缘由的 肯干，会让我们又开心又安心。

手记 4:

一个新测试员跑掉了一次。 用了几乎一整天才把他抓回测试 实验室。用了几乎一整天才把他抓 回测试实验室。实验室协调员斯科 特给他换上了一副新的"行头"。 斯科特随后把显示器的刷新率调 到让所有人眼前发黑，给他们一个 教训。 再出这种事，我得找克里斯和博谈 谈。至少，我们在他跑到当局之 前截住了他。

我打算下周再去市场上看看有没 有测试员可以挑。眼下还不需要， 但赶工时期我们消耗他们的速度 很快，多备几个调教好的总是好的 。 再说了，克里斯和博也需要练练手 。

DESIGNER DIARIES: FIRST SET

Darren Chukitus
Producer
Ghost Recon
Entry 1:

It has been an exciting month for the Ghost Recon team. We have finished our Alpha milestone and are plugging away at our push towards Beta. During this time I have been able to see the game evolve from what our team felt was necessary to make the game its best. We also have been able to take fan and focus group input to our meetings and determine how we can best serve everyone. A special thanks goes out to the people who provide us input on forums and through email. I personally don't get too much opportunity to chat on the forums, but let me let everyone know: we listen and appreciate your input. Thanks a lot!

I am extremely glad to have Greg Stelmack back with us on Ghost Recon and back with RSE. I have had the pleasure of working with Greg on RS Eagle Watch and I personally know him to be a great asset to our team and company. With 3 Stelmacks (the amazing interchangeable Stelmacks as I refer to them as), we have reached our Stelmack limit!

I just got back from LA, recording voice for the game. The folks at Soundelux studios have always treated us great-true pros in the industry. Bill Brown, composer for Ghost Recon, was excited to play me some new music cues we're working in for the game shell. This sound just fits perfectly. A touch of Russian themed instruments mixed with sensations of traditional American military music, Bill has touched on some new standards in game music. Between sessions, Dutch Hill (sound engineer) had set up a few guitars and processors for an impromptu jam session. Hendrix I'm not, but man, was that fun. Thanks Dutch!

Well, back to work. I just want to say the team is doing all it can to give you a great game. We'll be watching your posts on the forums.

Robbie Edwards - Associate Producer
Entry 1:

We've hit alpha. We have also run focus groups on Ghost Recon this month and will be analyzing all this data.We have a very stable and playable game at the moment and we're looking to add those last final features as we move towards our beta date. We're doing lots of demos for press guys so keep your eyes open on websites and magazines for articles talking about Ghost Recon. Most exciting is we have most of our sound assets now and the weapons in the game are sounding better than ever. Plus we've added a lot of the outstanding music our fans are used to and it adds so much to the game. All in all, the team is excited about the product and look forward to finishing it for all our fans.

Derek L Earwood
QA Analyst
Red Storm Entertainment
Entry 1:

Testing has finally resumed a more normal pace. With both test leads up to speed and a few testers on the project we can finally get something accomplished. It takes about 1 week to get new testers up to speed, the usual process of tedium followed up with verbal abuse, long hours and the fact they are working for free helps break their spirits and brings them into line with our way of thinking, in quick order. This tried and true process has never failed, and seems to be working wonders with the new guys. My Test Leads, Chris and Beau, are becoming masters at this. They make me so proud.

Entry 2:

The break in of the new testers is nearing completion. They seem without will most of the time now. The faint glimmer of independence I see in their eyes worries me some, but I have faith that too will soon be gone. Testing on a large project such as this takes mindless following of orders and I will not stand for people who think for themselves. Next they might start asking to take lunch breaks, go out for a smoke, or go to the bathroom. This will not be tolerated. The number of bugs they have been finding has gone up steadily as they lose the ability to think for themselves.

Entry 3:

I heard one of the testers say how much they enjoyed the endless testing of geometry and textures. This nearly brought tears to my eyes. Chris and Beau have done well. The engineers and artist seemed pleased with the work the new guys are doing. As we build up towards our next certification I am sure we will find the mindless enthusiasm of the testers a joy and comfort.

Entry 4:

One of the new testers escaped during a bathroom break. It took nearly all day to track him down and bring him back to the test lab. Our lab coordinator Scott brought out a new set of shackles for him.  Scott then set the refresh on the monitors to give them all blinding headaches as punishment. I will have to have a word with Chris and Beau if something like this happens again. At least we got the tester before he could get to the authorities.

I plan on going back to the auctions next week and seeing if there are any testers up for bid. We don't need them yet, but we tend to burn through them at a high rate during crunch times so it is always good to have a few spares that are already broken in. Besides, Chris and Beau need the practice.

一切都在正常推进，我们正走向 |Beta。到了这一步， |"正常"就意味着压力。 |全队都在拼命，确保一切赶上 |Beta，同时尽可能多玩这个游戏， |保证人人都玩得开心。可一天里就 |是没有足够的钟点把所有事做完。 |本地化工作占去了我大部分时间， |我还得帮着调整最后几个任务。 |我们很幸运，能在开发周期的早期 |就玩到自己的游戏，这给了我们大 |量时间做测试和玩法评估。 |我相信投入的所有心血最后都会 |体现在成品里。不过眼下， |只要能撑到 Beta...

加里斯特马克 (设计师)：
手记 1:

最近办公室里事情多得转不开身。 |我们正向 Beta 发起最后冲击， |这意味着要回应无数收尾事项， |填补我们没有预料到的空缺。 |大量功能总算要落进游戏里了， |事情进展顺利。本周内我们应该能 |完成所有单人任务的第一版， |带脚本要求的全部功能和一些玩 |法上的初步调整。到达 Beta 后， |不同难度的玩法调整就要动真格 |了。到那时 AI 功能将全部就位， |这会对最后的调整帮助极大。 |例行的内部任务会议给了大量有 |用的意见，最后的结果会是相当扎 |实的任务设计。在完整 3D |空间里看过之后， |好几个任务几乎被推倒重做--而每 |一处改动都是朝好的方向。

达伦丘基图斯 (制作人)
手记 1:

离幽灵行动的 Beta 还有几周， |进展相当不错。团队正在清掉待办 |清单，准备进入游戏的精修期。 |在开发的这一步，我们要求全队心 |往一处想，把手头的活干完。 |不难，对不对？！

幸好我们已经做了不少焦点小组 |和玩法评估，这会让最后的调整工 |作轻松一些。来自各方的意见应能 |让精修过程顺顺当当。大量好看的 |视觉特效在最近的版本里越来越 |多，很出色的音效也是。 |前几天我不声不响放了一段点 50 |机枪的声音，把一个记者惊得不轻 |。

重新设计是我们生产流程的重要 |一环。我们几乎用挑错的眼光审视 |过游戏的每个方面，来确定什么看 |起来最好、 |玩起来最好。团队和管理层能如此 |快速有效地处理重设计， |我深感幸运。希望玩家能在成品里 |看到这一点。

德里克厄尔伍德 (测试分析员)：
手记 1:

我发现美术师是非常敏感的人。 |你只要对某位说，他也许该想想改 |行--就算只是对他艺术才华的诚实 |评价--他们立刻就不乐意。 |家里那位也一样。你说实话， |家里那位身材该收紧了， |不然你很快就要换人了， |结果就是下巴挨了一记， |接下来六个星期只能靠管子过活。

总之，本周测试进展顺利。 |听说近期会有人来增援， |这能给我的两位测试组长克里斯 |和博减负。

手记 2:

克里斯和博最近好像压力很大。 |我跟他们说，再不收一收火气就把 |他们开除，可他们看起来还是静不 |下来。不知道还能如何帮他们放松 |。也许在实验室里多开几个通宵夜 |车、多起几个大早能帮他们振作起 |来。

手记 3:

我们被告知近期不许再加班了。 |另一件事：克里斯和博这周看起来 |开心多了。我跟他们说了， |接替他们的人快到了。这话让他们 |回到了现实，火气又回到了身上。 |这才是把活干对所需要的态度。 |火气。

手记 4:

本周一切安静。增援快到了。

Mike Haynes (美术组长)：
手记 1:

眼下我在做指挥地图，就是游戏里 |你为手下士兵标路径点时看到的 |那种图。我一开始还以为做这个很 |容易--大错特错。距离 Beta |还有一周。 |一切顺利。有几处地方需要改进， |还有几项特性要加进游戏， |但总体上节点在望。单人地图看起 |来好极了，关卡编辑们开始往地图 |里加特效，冲击力更上一层。UI |还需一些微调，但已经看得出在可 |用性、 |易用性和风格上下了大功夫。 |角色美术正在给人物做最后的修 |整，他们是我见过的所有游戏里最 |好的。整个团队都在持续交货， |游戏也因此看起来非常出色--这都 |是他们用心的成果。

埃里克阿姆斯特朗 (美术组长)：
手记 1:

挥起来，Bata，Bata，Bata，Bata|，Bataaaaaaaaaaa...挥！就是这|样。我只是在拼命 |赶完最后几个角色模型， |同时尽力保住常态。

John Sonedecker (美术组长)：
手记 1:

快到 Beta 了。这意味着什么？ |意味着做不完的活！ |有太多小东西必须在 Beta 前进 |游戏。我们把 Beta |定义为特性完成， |也就是说，所有在最后的游戏里该 |有的东西，那时就必须在游戏里。 |对关卡制作来说，这意味着所有关 |卡必须做完并进游戏。修 bug |和精修可以之后再做， |但游戏必须已在最后形态。
回去干活。一天里的每一分钟都算 |数！

Jeff Wesevich (软件工程师)
手记 1:

先从何处说起？带全新发射器能力 |的工具全部完工；几乎全部音效材 |料已经入库，任务和地图也正在显 |出最后形态。

天气是这个月的大更新， |特别是下雨。那里有不少好玩的效 |果，有些很微妙(打碎窗户会调高楼 |外雨声的音量)， |有些则不然(大雨天你藏在一块铁 |顶下面，就听不见有人靠近)。

工作量很大，但为每个任务"调制"|声 音环境也非常好玩。 |声音对了， 画面立刻上一个大步， |效果惊人。 :-)

战斗方面变化不大，不过我们换上 |了全数新武器声音。剪辑下了不少 |功夫，但效果一流。我曾看到 AI |队友用"机枪"朝一片区域乱扫， |把玩家惊得从座位上跳起来。

"友军"语音片段早就进游戏了， |这个月我们录了俄语声音并加了 进|去。我想给"坏蛋"们尽可能多的个 |性。这些片段不仅让不会说话的多 |边形和画面活了起来，而且， |打一个刚刚数落你三枪全空的家 |伙，就更有玩头。:-)

Beta 之后再聊...

Diana 斯特尔马克 (软件工程师)：
手记 1:

这是我参与的第一个游戏， |看着每个人出的力合在一起， |成一个完整的产品，到现在都很特 |别。干软件开发这一行这么多年， |我从没见过事情这么快就位。 |我等不及想看到成品了。

格雷格斯特尔马克 (软件工程师)
手记 1:

这个月很特别。我结束了在 Red |Storm 的9 个月"休假"， |一头扎回了幽灵行动的战团(这正 |是我当初离开时在做的项目)。 |从那以后它变了不少： |现在能玩了，而且好玩 ;-)

我一直在给团队当接球手。 |也就是说，我在接手那些没人直接 |负责的关键特性，比如回放、 |存档读档之类。我手头所有特性都 |已进游戏并在正常工作， |只是需要有人处理 bug， |并确保模式切换(开始回放、 |读档)不出错。

因为代码早就在我脑子里， |我没多少预备就被丢了进来。 |能回去做游戏编程真好。 |这里绝对是我该在的地方。

下个月再聊细节。

Jon Owen (软件工程师)
手记 1:

铁路桥：

我们在玩铁路桥任务， |团队对团队。美术师最近重做了这 |张地图，好看得很。 |他们还设置了几个不错的狙击位 |和机枪工事。敌人开局在一间小破 |房里，旁边就有机枪--不幸的是， |那是个狙击火力易及的位置。 |第一回合，我一口气冲向狙击位， |变焦看清--好家伙， |有人正在操枪。我切到 |M203，把榴弹一发发射过去。 |很险，但还没等他把枪口转到我这 |边，还没等他把枪口转过来， |那位枪手就被打瘫在地。哈哈。

山洞：

我们在合作玩山洞任务。 |我们一路横扫(我看是时候用精英 |难度玩这张图了)， 端掉营地， |活捉 Papashvili， |正带着残余敌人不多的态势前往 |撤离区。格雷大叫"左边小心！ |"，我立刻扑倒在地。 |格雷的子弹从我头顶上飞了过去 |，那个坏蛋(不对， |说错了，是"叛军")被爆了头。 |他一直藏在树后， |险些就报销了我。

当前进度：

人和火力组的 AI |已接近功能完成。 待办事项有：避|开动态物体(车辆)， |以及战斗撤退(这样队员们就能交 |替掩护、一段一段后撤)。

DESIGNER DIARIES: SECOND SET

Robbie Edwards (Associate Producer):
Entry 1:

Things are moving along normally as we progress towards beta. Normal at this stage in a project means filled with stress. The entire team is working hard to make sure everything gets in by beta along with playing the game as much as possible to ensure it's a game that everyone will enjoy. There just does not appear to be enough hours in the day to get everything done. Localization is taking up most of my time as well as trying to help balance those last few missions. We've been fortunate to be able to play our game early in the development cycle. That's allowed us lots of time for testing and game play evaluation. I'm sure all the hard work that's been put into this will show in the final product. But for now, if we can only get to beta....

Gary Stelmack (Designer):
Entry 1:

Life has been pretty hectic around the office lately. We are gearing up in the final push towards Beta, which means a lot of answering final questions, and filling in holes that we did not foresee. A lot of the functionality is just finally getting settled into the game, and things are coming along nicely. We should have our first pass on all the single player missions done by the end of this week. This includes all functionality from the script, and some initial play-balancing. Once we hit Beta, play-balancing for the different difficulties begin in earnest. We will finally have full AI functionality, which will help tremendously in the final play-balance. Our regular internal mission meetings have been providing plenty of good feedback. The end result will be very solid mission design. Several of the missions have been almost completely reworked once we got a look at the space in full 3D. In every case, the changes we have been making are for the better.

Darren Chukitus (Producer)
Entry 1:

A few more weeks to Beta of Ghost Recon and things are going pretty well. The team is wrapping up their list of to-dos, and getting organized to start the polish stage of the game. It is at this stage of our development process that we emphasize to the team focus and complete concentration on the tasks at hand. No problem, right?!

Fortunately we have had our share of focus groups and game play critiques that should make our life easier when we do some final play balancing. Input from all sides should make the polish process go smoothly. The wealth of special visual effects start showing up more in the current builds, as do some great sound effects. I scared a reporter pretty bad the other day when I caught him off guard with some of the .50 machine gun sounds.

Redesign has been a major part of our production process. We've practically looked at every aspect of our game with a critical eye to determine what looks and feels best. I feel fortunate that the team and management have been able to address the redesign aspect so quickly and effectively. I hope our fans see it in the final product.

Derek Earwood (QA Analyst):
Entry 1:

I have noticed artists are very sensitive people. You tell one that he should possibly find a different line of work…just as an honest evaluation of his artistic talents, and then they get all up in arms. The same goes for wives. You say something honest and meaningful like she needs to lose some weight or you will be replacing her real soon, and you end up with your jaw wired closed, eating dinner through a straw for the next 6 weeks.

Anywho. Testing has gone well this week.  I have been told we will be getting some additional assistance in the near future, which should take some workload off of my lead testers Chris and Beau.

Entry 2:

Chris and Beau seem to be under a lot of stress lately. I told them if they could not get a grip I was going to have them fired, but they still seem on edge. Not sure what else I can do to help them feel at ease.  Maybe more long nights and early mornings in the lab will help them get things together.

Entry 3:

We were told no more overtime for a while. On a different note Chris and Beau have seemed more cheerful this week.  I told them their replacements were arriving soon. This brought them back to earth, and got the surliness back in them. That is what they need to do the job right. Surliness.

Entry 4:

All has been quiet this week. Help is coming soon.

Mike Haynes (Lead Artist):
Entry 1:

At the moment I'm working on command maps; these are the maps you will see in game when you plot way points for your team of soldiers. My first thought was that creating them would be easy, man was I wrong. We're one week away from Beta. Everything is going well. We have a few areas that need improvements and a few more features to put in the game, but overall we're looking good for the milestone. The single player maps are looking awesome, level builders are starting to add FX to their maps and it's adding that extra punch.UI has a few more tweaks but should show that a lot of attention was paid to usability, ease of use and style. The character artists are putting the final touches on the characters and they are turning out the best I've seen in any game. Through and through the team is continuing to deliver the goods, and the game is looking great as a result of their hard work.

Eric Armstrong (Lead Artist):
Entry 1:

Hey Bata, Bata, Bata, Bata, Bataaaaaaaaaaa...........Swing! That's about it. Just trying to crank out these last remaining character models and still retain my sanity.

John Sonedecker (Lead Artist):
Entry 1:

Almost Beta. What does that mean? Well, lots and lots of work! There are so many little things that need to get into the game for Beta. We define Beta as feature complete and that means that if it is going to be in the final game it must be represented in the game at that time. On the level building side it means that we must have all levels completed and in the game. Bug fixing and polish can come later, but the game must be in its final form.
Back to work. All minutes in the day count!

Jeff Wesevich (Software Engineer)
Entry 1:

Hmmm....where to begin? The tools with all the new emitter capabilities have been finished up; almost all of the sound assets are in and the mission and maps are resolving into their final forms.

Weather was one of the big additions this month, in particular rain. There are a number of interesting effects there, some of which are subtle (shooting out a window raises the volume on the rain coming from outside the building) and others not (you won't hear anyone walking up if you're hiding under a tin roof in a heavy rain).

It's been a lot of work, but also a lot of fun to "sculpt" the sound environments for each mission.It's amazing how much better the graphics look when the sound is right. :-)

Not much has changed on the combat front, although we did get all new weapon sounds. It took quite a bit of editing, but the results are outstanding. I've seen nearby AI teammates hosing down the area with a "saw" cause players to come out of their chairs..

The "friendly" voice clips have been in for a while, but we recorded and added the Russian voices this month. I want to give the "bad guys" as much personality as I can. Not only do the clips add life to the mute polys and textures, it's just plain more fun to shoot someone who's been laughing and taunting you because your last 3 shots missed. :-)

More after Beta....

Diana Stelmack (Software Engineer):
Entry 1:

This being my first game, it has been interesting so far to see how the individual efforts come together to make a cohesive product. In my entire software development career, I have not seen things fall together so quickly. I can't wait to see the finished product.

Greg Stelmack (Software Engineer)
Entry 1:

Well, this has been an interesting month. I'm back from my 9 month vacation from Red Storm and have been thrown right back into the Ghost Recon fray (which is what I was working on when I left originally). It's changed quite a bit since then: now it's playable and fun ;-)

I've been playing catcher for the team. That means I'm picking up some of the key features that didn't have anyone with directly assigned responsibilities. Things like replay, save/load game, and the like. All the features I have are in and working, they just needed someone to handle the bugs and make sure the mode changes (starting a replay, loading a game) don't have any issues.

Since I'm familiar with the code base, I just got thrown right in without much warmup time. It's been great to get back into game coding. This is definitely where I belong.

More details next month.

Jon Owen (Software Engineer)
Entry 1:

RR Bridge:

We were playing the railroad bridge mission team vs. team. The artists have recently redone the map and it looks gorgeous. They also put in some good sniping positions and machinegun emplacements. The enemy was starting at a shack near a machinegun, and unfortunately for them, in a place vulnerable to sniper fire. In the first round, I beat feet over to the sniper position, zoomed in, and lo and behold, someone was manning the gun. I switched to my M203 and walked in some frags. It was close, but the gunner was turned to jelly before he brought his gun to bear on me. Muhuhahaha.

Caves:

We were playing the caves mission co-op. We roared through the mission (I think it's time we start playing this one on Elite), wiping out the camp, capturing Papashvili, and were on our way to the extraction zone with only light enemy forces remaining. Greg yelled "ON YOUR LEFT!", and I hit the dirt. Greg's fire went right over my head and the tango (er, sorry "rebel") took it in the head. He'd been hidden behind a tree and was just about to wax me.

Current stuff:

The human and fireteam ai are darned near feature complete. Things left to do include avoiding dynamic objects (vehicles), and fighting retreat (so guys will do bounding overwatch with cover to the rear).

大卫哈姆，软件工程师

手记 1:

幽灵行动团队很大。有时候确实显 |得太大了。就算是开放办公， |我们也塞不满一个大房间--工程师 |进不了同一个房间。这就要求我们 |在交流上想点办法。工作区里有大 |量随机起意的交谈，而且谈着谈着 |就会把旁人拖进来。这有时让人不 |快， |因为我安静的环境里效率更高。 |但这么大的项目， |就得做这种取舍。 |跟我当年在大学房间里独自开夜 |车编程的日子相比， |变化真是不小。

真要专心做一个明确的功能时， |我学会了用音乐隔绝干扰。 |代价是错失几个电话，不过那些电 |话多半本来就是从语音留言系统 |里打错分机的人打来的。 |有时候我想，管理层老让我转接电 |话，是不是该让他们付点什么。 |可我大概也不知道如何正确转接 |电话，那就算了。总之，我听 |Metallica 的时候， |同事们有事只能跑过来招手提问。 |希望他们别太介意。

Diana 斯特尔马克，软件工程师

手记 1:

合作任务把我们都放进同一个队 |伍，在单人战役的一个任务里一起 |对抗坏蛋。这种玩法很快成了我的 |最爱。它让任务有了和单人完全不 |同的体验。总之， |开口没个把门的，人人玩得开心， |人人都玩得很开心。

手记 2:

作为 Red Storm |家属，这次的赶工远没有过去 |那些赶工那么受罪(那时候我只能 |待在家里，算着丈夫长 day |工作后几点才能把自己拖回家)。 |我们挨过一些长夜， |我这周也特别长(到现在大约 11 |天了)，但等最后的游戏做成、 |成为我们都拿得出手的东西， |一切都值得。

John Sonedecker (美术组长， |关卡)

手记 1:

我的头正在遭罪。前几天打 |hockey，有人一记大力击球正中 |我两眼之间。我直接被人撞翻在场 |地里！好在有 helmet 护着， |但还是被撞得不轻， |右眼上方也挨了一下。

对了，幽灵行动。我们到达 Beta |了，游戏好极了。我难免护短， |但它看起来、玩起来都难以置信。 |最有说服力的是：那些本来不喜欢 |R6/RS 风格玩法的 RSE 同事 |，玩起幽灵行动来 和我们这些 |R6/RS 死忠一样投入！ |等不及看玩家的反应，希望能带来 |一批新的支持者， |听听他们的反应。

关卡方面，我们在修 bug、精修、 |再精修。担心早期截图里"多边 |形"石头的朋友可以放心了。 |我认识的最出色的工程师之一， |Philip H.，没有增加一个 |多边形就把麻烦解决了。 |谢了，Philip。

我更新了一批武器模型， |效果很好。角色组的家伙们在做一 |个强得不得了的狙击手角色， |我把他的步枪配上了--各位， |先缓一口气--Ghillie 服！ |难以置信。我们试玩"找狙击手"， |大多数人都找不到。 |不过放心，这个角色会做强度调整 |，不会永远是最优选择， |也不会"统治"整张地图。

手记 2:

游戏快完成了，我正全力让关卡做 |到最好。

我又在读 Black Hawk |Down。它把身处真实军事行动 |中央的感受讲得非常好。 |每次读这类文字，都觉得自己没碰 |上那种处境实在是运气。 |对上过那种战场的人，我打心底里 |佩服。

加里斯特马克，设计师

手记 1:

过去两周发生了很多事。 |游戏正式到达 Beta。 |对我们做设计的人来说， |精修期开始了。我们正在给难 |度做脚本。每周每人给两个任务做 |难度。到了周四，交换任务试玩， |然后碰头互提批评和意见。 |最后，隔天落实必要的修改， |下周再让四个关卡走同样的流程。

简而言之，从 Beta 到第一个 GM |候选版的这段日子事情很多， |但必不可少。所有任务都都已按应 |有的行为设置就位： |胜利条件、特别脚本事件都已就位 |了。现在只需为不同难度变换脚本 |。处理各难度脚本区分的方式有好 |几种，最简单的是增减兵力， |但工具不止这一个。我们真的可以 |按正在游玩的难度排入成块的脚 |本，这让关卡脚本作者可以在难度 |编排上玩出各种变化：也许增援会 |来得更早，也许那个家伙跑到警报 |开关的距 |离会更短。一切都有可能。

手记 2:

我们已经在通往 GM 的路上。 |到目前为止，游戏真的开始成形了 |。团队里的人能多玩一些了， |意见非常积极。看到新闻界的试玩 |报道和他们对幽灵行动的期待， |很让人受用。

对我们做设计的人来说， |流程在变。我们已全职转入任务修 b|ug，并给玩法调整做最后一道修整|。 |到目前为止，调整方面的意见相当 |不错。看来最后一个任务在新兵难 |度下需要稍微收一收，但总体上， |玩起来的感觉正中我们当初的设 |计。

团队也开始有了自己的战争往事， |我看他们快要去跟 AI |程序员说道说 道了。AI |正变得精明得惊人。 |你用狙击枪瞄住一个人， |只能眼看着发射出去的榴弹在准 |星里越来越大--因为目标正在把你 |刚做过的事原样送回给你。

看到所有部分如此利落地各就各 |位，实在让人受用。

Mike Haynes，美术组长 (多人、 |UI、特效)

手记 1:

好了，Beta |之后，最后的收尾...向 Gold |进发。 |我们已经能看到尽头的那道光， |而且非常亮。游戏看起来好极了， |这里很多人都在加班加点， |确保幽灵行动会大获成功。 |关卡非常了得，我敢说我们的人物 |是到今天为止所有游戏里最好看 |的。希望玩家也这么看。 |我们还有路要走， |但一切都要靠精修。如果游戏在 |Beta 就已经这么好看， |我真等不及看 Gold 版了。 |我一直在专心做指挥地图--就是游 |戏里看到的那种从上往下看的图 |--力求做出一致、真实的效果。

手记 2:

距 GM 两周。一切顺利， |全队都围着修 bug 转。 |每个新版本质量都在上升， |很提气。我正在处理指挥地图的几 |个麻烦，并确保多人地图和主界面 |里的一切都正确。种种信号都表明 |这个游戏会大获成功，团队应当为 |把游戏带到这个地步而自豪。 |接下来， 是更多的深夜和修 |bug...

罗比爱德华兹，副制作人

手记 1:

Beta 总算到了！团队为达成 Beta |目标拼尽了全力。这一天到来时， |我们发现游戏基本完成了 99% |的特性。这意味着项目 |剩下的工作只是修 bug 和精修。 |这直接等于给玩家的成品会好得 |多。我相信他们都会发现这是一个 |精心制作、用心设计的游戏。 |每个任务都是与众不同的独特挑 |战，不同于我们或任何其他公司做 |过的任何游戏。上周几乎全队每晚 |都干到午夜，还有几个人索性住在 |公司，只合眼几个小时。 |但我确信，产品出货、 |人人上手的时候， |他们会体会到团队付出的心血。 |好了，回去干活，还剩几个星期。

手记 2:

过去几周团队事情多得转不开身。 |我们在压低 bug 数量， |好拿出一个扎实的 Gold 候选版。 |我大部分时间用在照料全队日常 |所需上。不算体面， |但我想总要紧。同时尽可能多玩游 |戏，确保所有 bug |都被找到并修掉。 |还在做最后几个关头的建议--让克 |拉克受不了，但让游戏更好。 |现在我们都需要好心情， |人人都在加班，压力把每个人都压 |得很紧。不过大概一切都会好起来 |的。很快我们就能完工了。

达伦丘基图斯，制作人

手记 1:

团队又连轴转了一周--Beta。 |好极了！幽灵行动的全部特性总算 |到位，我们可以着手给游戏做玩法 |调整了。

最近来了很多新闻界的人， |看过的人看起来都很开心。 |好处是，尽管我们让新闻界玩了 |Beta，但他们看到的并非全部。 |Beta 的意义在于把一切调试正常， |有时那些好看的特性并不会随时 |显示出来。新闻界会玩一个任务， |但玩不到整个战役。或者， |有时关键在于解锁你最喜欢的专 |家。

幽灵行动里几乎每项特性都需要 |继续精修，这样才能给玩家完整、 |能让人投入的体验。举个例子， |我们对环境里的树木就是如此， |不断试验新手法，让它们看起来正 |合适。角色也是一样： |确保它们看起来正合适、 |动作和外观足够真实， |这些活我们会一直干到时间用尽。

请放心：光是这游戏的整体观感， |就足以让玩家得到极大的满足。

德里克厄尔伍德，测试组长

手记 1:

留给测试团队的时间不多了。 |我从组员的眼里看出了绝望。Beau |被指派从现在到项目结束只做一 |件事：bug |回退。对我这支人数不多、 |又不太会来往的测试队伍来说， |手头的活还算好玩， |但也相当不易。 |我的得力助手克里斯清楚局势的 |真相，也清楚它有多无望。Beau |也清楚，但每天例行的回退活已经 |开始消耗他的脑子。除此之外， |一切都好。

手记 2:

时间一天天过去，意味着， |我们剩下的测试时间比上一周更 |短了。要不是测试间里如今人人手 |边都有点压惊的东西，这本来会让 |人有点低落。每当他被派更多回退 |活时，Beau |眼里的样子在我看来是个好信号 |。测试这边，我们觉得时间很紧， |一种平静的绝望感正在慢慢罩下 |来，但总体上，事情还在推进。

这样的项目难免有几个小插曲。 |幽灵行动也不例外。过去一周， |工程室里又爆发了一场关于蓝色 |二极管之争。两边都死守自己的论 |点，没有一方想让步。 |这件事压了几周， |就等着爆发，所以没有人对它的 |到来感到意外。项目制作人达伦迅 |速介入，想把争端按下去。 |交战各方被拉开， |两边损失都不大。 |没有人想再见识一次 2000 |年的chimichanga 事件--那 |场事变以一场几乎不流血的政变 |收场，把团队原来的头号工程师赶 |了下去。这事就说到此为止。 |除此之外，一切都好。

埃里克阿姆斯特朗，美术组长

手记 1:

呼--最难的部分过去了！ |现在我们可 以松一口气修 bug |了。 过去一个月左右 |我们非常专注： 通宵达旦， |中间只合眼一到两小时 ， |但值了。看看现在， |再对比三个月前， |简直一个天上一个地下。 |我翻了翻以前的角色截图， |跟新的比了比，下巴都惊掉了！ |角色团队在这个项目里学到了太 |多。我们一定会把这些经验用到接 |下来的项目里。从今往后， |只会越做越好！

开发手记：第三辑

格雷格斯特尔马克，软件工程师

手记 1:

Diana 刚把合作模式跑通， 我们只好帮着测试。 真是开心。有了战术 AI 的改进， 我们真得协同作战了。我悄悄绕到 侧翼，等队友和敌人交火后， 就从侧面一个接一个点名。 我们让榴弹飞进敌营，另有人架好 枪拦截逃跑的家伙。团队合作真正 打了出来，玩得非常开心。 这个游戏真的越看越有模样。

手记 2:

向 Beta 冲击的这几天事情很多。 大量特性往里塞，新特性一来就会 破坏一波，于是要做大量修复。 今天的多人对战测试很好。 我对着雾里的枪口火光开枪， 从窗户往里投榴弹对付机枪手(不 过得小心别打在窗台以下...)， 还到处绕到别人侧后。一次合作任 务里，我在清路这边， 别人在清对面，结果我先完工。 我过了铁路桥到对面， 正撞上朝战友不停开火的敌人 的背后。那场面就像 Sgt. York 里的镜头， 我沿着队列把他们一个个点掉。 大家都玩得开心。

手记 3:

修 bug 去，修 bug 去
修 bug 去，修 bug 去
Hi-ho the derry-o
修 bug 去，修 bug 去

手记 4:

我在玩任务 2，想重现一个战役崩溃 。 我装上小队插入战场。 照例打开夜 视， 命令一个小队推进到山脊北端 并向下掩护以防我陷入麻烦， 然后带着另一队直插进去清剿。

我来到山脊开始往上爬， 保持一定的小心。刚要翻上脊线， 就看见两个敌方巡逻兵正从左到 右走在山背面。我开始仔细瞄准， 可是领头的用余光发现了我， 转身举枪。我放倒他， 再转向他旁边那位。 那家伙缩到了树后面， 我开始扫射。装弹时， 一个球状物体从树里飞出来。 一个队友大叫"小心！ "，我随即前冲(手雷已经飞过去了)， 绕过树身，朝哨兵一通乱打。 他倒下了。

可我的威胁指示器仍显示附近有 人。也许是另一支巡逻队赶来看情 况。于是我蹲下， 慢慢潜行绕回树后。 突然，一个俄语声音几乎就在我头 顶，然后我就中了枪。 那家伙开枪之前还损了我一下 ;-)

玩游戏玩得太开心了。我最好回去 老实找 bug、修 bug，不然克拉克要生气了...

手记 5:

我修好了读档时的战役崩溃。 又一次。而且多半还得再修一次。 又一次。

手记 6:

我把 bug 单里由昨天回退引出的错处 清掉了。我实在反感回退。 希望它们永远别再回来。

Jon Owen，软件工程师

手记 1:

做 AI 的时候，你有时会碰上我们称之 为"自发生出的行为"的东西。 大致就是一个系统表现出比组成 它的子系统更复杂的行为。 最近就有两个例子：

Jeff 给坏蛋们录了大量语音。 他们会向你叫阵、 聊天，有时还会自言自语， 等等。我们最近给 AI 加上了对 这些声音作出反应的能力。 第一个任务的特别目标， 是活捉一个藏身山洞的叛军头目。 你端掉他的手下后，他会投降并可 以让他跟着你。他跟着你的时候几 乎说个不停。 我不知道他在说什么，但我的 AI 队友显然被气着了--俘虏一 开口，我的 AI 战友就转过身来， 把 M16 直直指着他。 看起来还不坏， 但他们在原地打转上用掉的时间 太多，过地图太慢， 所以我关掉了对俘虏声音的反应。

另一个例子是安全持枪。美术师 Sloan 指出，让队友端着枪、 枪口永远平对着自己人站在那里， 看起来非常不安全。我当过 NRA 的小会员， 于是决定：当火力组队友在前方 时，让他们把枪举起来。 负责动作的 Joe 已经有一段"别让枪进到墙里"的代 码，会让士兵举枪。 我这人天生图省事，就直接接进了 Joe 的代码里。 Joe 那段实际上要做 3D 几何碰撞检查来 判断枪有没有顶到东西， 所以他得小心别让它占用太多运 算周期。他小心地把检查限制在角 色正被显示的时刻--你不看的时候 ，就不用做检测。 这对我的代码意味着： 你不看着队友时，他们会开开心 心地把枪口对准你。

你一转身，他们几乎总正在举枪。 看上去就像他们在想"要不要给这 位长官来一发榴弹"。 Jeff 看到后，当然想让他们在你没看的 时候小声说点威胁的话。

Jeff Wesevich，软件工程师

Alex："没关系，Daddy。"

大卫哈姆，软件工程师

手记 1:

幽灵行动团队很大。有时候确实显 得太大了。就算是开放办公， 我们也塞不满一个大房间--工程师 进不了同一个房间。这就要求我们 在交流上想点办法。工作区里有大 量随机起意的交谈，而且谈着谈着 就会把旁人拖进来。这有时让人不 快， 因为我安静的环境里效率更高。 但这么大的项目， 就得做这种取舍。 跟我当年在大学房间里独自开夜 车编程的日子相比， 变化真是不小。

真要专心做一个明确的功能时， 我学会了用音乐隔绝干扰。 代价是错失几个电话，不过那些电 话多半本来就是从语音留言系统 里打错分机的人打来的。 有时候我想，管理层老让我转接电 话，是不是该让他们付点什么。 可我大概也不知道如何正确转接 电话，那就算了。总之，我听 Metallica 的时候， 同事们有事只能跑过来招手提问。 希望他们别太介意。

Diana 斯特尔马克，软件工程师

手记 1:

合作任务把我们都放进同一个队 伍，在单人战役的一个任务里一起 对抗坏蛋。这种玩法很快成了我的 最爱。它让任务有了和单人完全不 同的体验。总之， 开口没个把门的，人人玩得开心， 人人都玩得很开心。

手记 2:

作为 Red Storm 家属，这次的赶工远没有过去 那些赶工那么受罪(那时候我只能 待在家里，算着丈夫长 day 工作后几点才能把自己拖回家)。 我们挨过一些长夜， 我这周也特别长(到现在大约 11 天了)，但等最后的游戏做成、 成为我们都拿得出手的东西， 一切都值得。

John Sonedecker (美术组长， 关卡)

手记 1:

我的头正在遭罪。前几天打 hockey，有人一记大力击球正中 我两眼之间。我直接被人撞翻在场 地里！好在有 helmet 护着， 但还是被撞得不轻， 右眼上方也挨了一下。

对了，幽灵行动。我们到达 Beta 了，游戏好极了。我难免护短， 但它看起来、玩起来都难以置信。 最有说服力的是：那些本来不喜欢 R6/RS 风格玩法的 RSE 同事 ，玩起幽灵行动来 和我们这些 R6/RS 死忠一样投入！ 等不及看玩家的反应，希望能带来 一批新的支持者， 听听他们的反应。

关卡方面，我们在修 bug、精修、 再精修。担心早期截图里"多边 形"石头的朋友可以放心了。 我认识的最出色的工程师之一， Philip H.，没有增加一个 多边形就把麻烦解决了。 谢了，Philip。

我更新了一批武器模型， 效果很好。角色组的家伙们在做一 个强得不得了的狙击手角色， 我把他的步枪配上了--各位， 先缓一口气--Ghillie 服！ 难以置信。我们试玩"找狙击手"， 大多数人都找不到。 不过放心，这个角色会做强度调整 ，不会永远是最优选择， 也不会"统治"整张地图。

手记 2:

游戏快完成了，我正全力让关卡做 到最好。

我又在读 Black Hawk Down。它把身处真实军事行动 中央的感受讲得非常好。 每次读这类文字，都觉得自己没碰 上那种处境实在是运气。 对上过那种战场的人，我打心底里 佩服。

加里斯特马克，设计师

手记 1:

过去两周发生了很多事。 游戏正式到达 Beta。 对我们做设计的人来说， 精修期开始了。我们正在给难 度做脚本。每周每人给两个任务做 难度。到了周四，交换任务试玩， 然后碰头互提批评和意见。 最后，隔天落实必要的修改， 下周再让四个关卡走同样的流程。

简而言之，从 Beta 到第一个 GM 候选版的这段日子事情很多， 但必不可少。所有任务都都已按应 有的行为设置就位： 胜利条件、特别脚本事件都已就位 了。现在只需为不同难度变换脚本 。处理各难度脚本区分的方式有好 几种，最简单的是增减兵力， 但工具不止这一个。我们真的可以 按正在游玩的难度排入成块的脚 本，这让关卡脚本作者可以在难度 编排上玩出各种变化：也许增援会 来得更早，也许那个家伙跑到警报 开关的距 离会更短。一切都有可能。

手记 2:

我们已经在通往 GM 的路上。 到目前为止，游戏真的开始成形了 。团队里的人能多玩一些了， 意见非常积极。看到新闻界的试玩 报道和他们对幽灵行动的期待， 很让人受用。

对我们做设计的人来说， 流程在变。我们已全职转入任务修 bug，并给玩法调整做最后一道修整。 到目前为止，调整方面的意见相当 不错。看来最后一个任务在新兵难 度下需要稍微收一收，但总体上， 玩起来的感觉正中我们当初的设 计。

团队也开始有了自己的战争往事， 我看他们快要去跟 AI 程序员说道说 道了。AI 正变得精明得惊人。 你用狙击枪瞄住一个人， 只能眼看着发射出去的榴弹在准 星里越来越大--因为目标正在把你 刚做过的事原样送回给你。

看到所有部分如此利落地各就各 位，实在让人受用。

Mike Haynes，美术组长 (多人、 UI、特效)

手记 1:

好了，Beta 之后，最后的收尾...向 Gold 进发。 我们已经能看到尽头的那道光， 而且非常亮。游戏看起来好极了， 这里很多人都在加班加点， 确保幽灵行动会大获成功。 关卡非常了得，我敢说我们的人物 是到今天为止所有游戏里最好看 的。希望玩家也这么看。 我们还有路要走， 但一切都要靠精修。如果游戏在 Beta 就已经这么好看， 我真等不及看 Gold 版了。 我一直在专心做指挥地图--就是游 戏里看到的那种从上往下看的图 --力求做出一致、真实的效果。

手记 2:

距 GM 两周。一切顺利， 全队都围着修 bug 转。 每个新版本质量都在上升， 很提气。我正在处理指挥地图的几 个麻烦，并确保多人地图和主界面 里的一切都正确。种种信号都表明 这个游戏会大获成功，团队应当为 把游戏带到这个地步而自豪。 接下来， 是更多的深夜和修 bug...

罗比爱德华兹，副制作人

手记 1:

Beta 总算到了！团队为达成 Beta 目标拼尽了全力。这一天到来时， 我们发现游戏基本完成了 99% 的特性。这意味着项目 剩下的工作只是修 bug 和精修。 这直接等于给玩家的成品会好得 多。我相信他们都会发现这是一个 精心制作、用心设计的游戏。 每个任务都是与众不同的独特挑 战，不同于我们或任何其他公司做 过的任何游戏。上周几乎全队每晚 都干到午夜，还有几个人索性住在 公司，只合眼几个小时。 但我确信，产品出货、 人人上手的时候， 他们会体会到团队付出的心血。 好了，回去干活，还剩几个星期。

手记 2:

过去几周团队事情多得转不开身。 我们在压低 bug 数量， 好拿出一个扎实的 Gold 候选版。 我大部分时间用在照料全队日常 所需上。不算体面， 但我想总要紧。同时尽可能多玩游 戏，确保所有 bug 都被找到并修掉。 还在做最后几个关头的建议--让克 拉克受不了，但让游戏更好。 现在我们都需要好心情， 人人都在加班，压力把每个人都压 得很紧。不过大概一切都会好起来 的。很快我们就能完工了。

达伦丘基图斯，制作人

手记 1:

团队又连轴转了一周--Beta。 好极了！幽灵行动的全部特性总算 到位，我们可以着手给游戏做玩法 调整了。

最近来了很多新闻界的人， 看过的人看起来都很开心。 好处是，尽管我们让新闻界玩了 Beta，但他们看到的并非全部。 Beta 的意义在于把一切调试正常， 有时那些好看的特性并不会随时 显示出来。新闻界会玩一个任务， 但玩不到整个战役。或者， 有时关键在于解锁你最喜欢的专 家。

幽灵行动里几乎每项特性都需要 继续精修，这样才能给玩家完整、 能让人投入的体验。举个例子， 我们对环境里的树木就是如此， 不断试验新手法，让它们看起来正 合适。角色也是一样： 确保它们看起来正合适、 动作和外观足够真实， 这些活我们会一直干到时间用尽。

请放心：光是这游戏的整体观感， 就足以让玩家得到极大的满足。

德里克厄尔伍德，测试组长

手记 1:

留给测试团队的时间不多了。 我从组员的眼里看出了绝望。Beau 被指派从现在到项目结束只做一 件事：bug 回退。对我这支人数不多、 又不太会来往的测试队伍来说， 手头的活还算好玩， 但也相当不易。 我的得力助手克里斯清楚局势的 真相，也清楚它有多无望。Beau 也清楚，但每天例行的回退活已经 开始消耗他的脑子。除此之外， 一切都好。

手记 2:

时间一天天过去，意味着， 我们剩下的测试时间比上一周更 短了。要不是测试间里如今人人手 边都有点压惊的东西，这本来会让 人有点低落。每当他被派更多回退 活时，Beau 眼里的样子在我看来是个好信号 。测试这边，我们觉得时间很紧， 一种平静的绝望感正在慢慢罩下 来，但总体上，事情还在推进。

这样的项目难免有几个小插曲。 幽灵行动也不例外。过去一周， 工程室里又爆发了一场关于蓝色 二极管之争。两边都死守自己的论 点，没有一方想让步。 这件事压了几周， 就等着爆发，所以没有人对它的 到来感到意外。项目制作人达伦迅 速介入，想把争端按下去。 交战各方被拉开， 两边损失都不大。 没有人想再见识一次 2000 年的chimichanga 事件--那 场事变以一场几乎不流血的政变 收场，把团队原来的头号工程师赶 了下去。这事就说到此为止。 除此之外，一切都好。

埃里克阿姆斯特朗，美术组长

手记 1:

呼--最难的部分过去了！ 现在我们可 以松一口气修 bug 了。 过去一个月左右 我们非常专注： 通宵达旦， 中间只合眼一到两小时 ， 但值了。看看现在， 再对比三个月前， 简直一个天上一个地下。 我翻了翻以前的角色截图， 跟新的比了比，下巴都惊掉了！ 角色团队在这个项目里学到了太 多。我们一定会把这些经验用到接 下来的项目里。从今往后， 只会越做越好！
